topic.title: Salary screenshots without the years
topic.claim: A ₹35 LPA screenshot is a highlight reel, and we compare ourselves to it without ever asking how many switches it took.
topic.behaviour: People scroll salary threads and LinkedIn posts, see a big number and feel behind, while skipping the starting salary, the age and the number of job changes.
topic.mechanism: Comparison needs a clean number, and context makes it messy. We prefer the version of someone's career that makes our own look slow, because it's easier to feel behind than to find out what the real path looked like.
real_details: A thread asks people to share role, first salary, current salary and age
The opening example is a product designer who went from 3 LPA to 35 LPA by age 28
The stated aim is to show what it took to reach a figure like 70 LPA
The OP says it might be 10 years or 3 years with 6 job switches
The post was popular enough that the OP edited to say it blew up
topic.why_now: Appraisal and switching season makes everyone check other people's numbers.

score.why: Named, specific screenshot flex that replaces the car/house humble-brag, same lane as the mutual-fund-screenshot take he kept.

sources.fact: Entry-level IT pay in India is about ₹3–4 LPA, so a ₹35 LPA figure is many multiples of where most careers start.
sources.excerpt: In 2026, the same position pays around Rs 3.36 lakh per annum, according to Careers360, a rise of just Rs 20,000 annually over nearly nineteen years. | Entry-level packages at Infosys, Wipro and multinational firms such as Accenture largely remain in the Rs 3–4 LPA range. | Base salaries for freshers have barely changed in close to two decades.

sources.fact: Aon projects the average annual raise in India at 9.1% for 2026, so staying in one job grows pay slowly and big jumps usually come from other routes.
sources.excerpt: India's average salary increase is projected to rise slightly to 9.1% in 2026, up from 8.9% in 2025 | Overall attrition fell to 16.2% in 2025, down from 17.7% in 2024 and 18.7% in 2023

sources.fact: In foundit's 2026 survey, most professionals expect a 21% or larger raise when they switch jobs, which shows that switching drives big salary jumps.
sources.excerpt: 70% of professionals expect a salary increase of 21% or more from a new employer, with 27% seeking a 21–30% jump. | One in five professionals expects a salary bump of more than 40% when switching jobs | just 7% of respondents said they would consider moving for a hike of less than 10% | a single-digit salary hike may not be enough to make the move worthwhile.

paragraphs: Freshers in IT still start around 3 to 4 LPA. Raises average 9.1%. So how is someone your age already on 35?
You're missing everything except the last number.
A 35 LPA figure comes without the first salary, the age, or how many offer letters it took.
Comparison needs a clean number. Context makes it messy, so it gets cropped out.
Most IT careers start small. Freshers at Infosys, Wipro and Accenture still get around 3 to 4 LPA.
Then comes the yearly raise. Aon projects the 2026 average raise at 9.1%.
Nobody climbs to 35 on 9.1% a year.
The jump comes from leaving. 70% of professionals expect 21% or more from a new employer.
So the same 35 LPA might be ten years. Or three years and six switches.
And honestly, most people don't want the full story.
The full story has notice periods, new bosses, a fresh onboarding every year and a resume that looks restless.
Feeling behind is easier. It doesn't ask you to update your CV.
So when a 35 LPA screenshot lands in your group chat, ask the boring question.
How many jobs did that take? And how old were they at the first resignation mail?

draft.caption: What was your first salary, and how many switches did it take to get to what you earn now?
draft.alt_text: A six-slide text carousel about comparing yourself to big salary numbers during appraisal season. It says a 35 LPA figure hides the starting salary, age and number of job switches. It notes fresher IT pay is still around 3 to 4 LPA, the average raise for 2026 is projected at 9.1%, and most professionals expect 21% or more when switching. It ends by suggesting you ask how many jobs a big number took.

hook_candidates.hook: Freshers in IT still start around 3 to 4 LPA. Raises average 9.1%. So how is someone your age already on 35?
That 35 LPA screenshot in your group chat could be ten years of work. Or three. And you can't tell which.
Imagine starting on 4 LPA and getting a 9.1% raise every single year. Now guess how long it takes to reach 35.
Appraisal season makes you feel slow because someone your age is on 35 LPA. The number left out is the one that matters.
A 35 LPA salary screenshot is a highlight reel. It shows the last number and cuts out every job before it.
